payload.content: The following are not inventions within the meaning of this Act: an invention which in effect, is traditional knowledge or which is an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known component or components. In Ayurvedic applications, claims attempting to patent classical formulations or known traditional medicinal uses of plants (documented in classical texts or TKDL) are barred under this section.
payload.source: The Patents Act, 1970 (India)
payload.topic: Patents & Traditional Knowledge Exclusions
payload.version: As amended by Patents (Amendment) Act, 2005 & Rules 2024
payload.heading: Inventions not patentable: Traditional Knowledge and Aggregation
payload.authority: Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), India

payload.content: A substance obtained by a mere admixture resulting only in the aggregation of the properties of the components thereof or a process for producing such substance is not patentable. For poly-herbal Ayurvedic formulations, applicants must provide verifiable pharmacological or clinical data proving non-obvious synergistic interaction between the herbs beyond the sum of individual actions.
payload.source: The Patents Act, 1970 (India)
payload.topic: Patents & Traditional Knowledge Exclusions
payload.heading: Inventions not patentable: Mere Admixture without Synergism

payload.content: The mere discovery of a new form of a known substance which does not result in the enhancement of the known efficacy of that substance or the mere discovery of any new property or new use for a known substance or of the mere use of a known process, machine or apparatus unless such known process results in a new product or employs at least one new reactant. In Ayurvedic derivatives, enhancement of therapeutic efficacy must be experimentally established.
payload.source: The Patents Act, 1970 (India)
payload.topic: Patents & Traditional Knowledge Exclusions
payload.heading: Inventions not patentable: New forms or new uses of known substances

payload.content: An invention means a new product or process involving an inventive step and capable of industrial application. In Ayurvedic processing, novel standardized extraction methods, specific fractionations, or novel delivery systems (such as nano-liposomes, phytosomes, or emulgels) can meet this criterion if not previously disclosed in classical literature.
payload.source: The Patents Act, 1970 (India)
payload.topic: Patents & Traditional Knowledge Exclusions
payload.heading: Definition of Invention: Novelty and Inventive Step

payload.content: Every complete specification shall disclose the source and geographical origin of the biological material in the specification, when that used for the invention is from India. Failure to disclose or wrongful disclosure constitutes statutory grounds for pre-grant opposition, post-grant opposition, or patent revocation under Section 64.
payload.source: The Patents Act, 1970 (India)
payload.topic: Patents & Traditional Knowledge Exclusions
payload.heading: Contents of Specification: Mandatory Biological Material Origin Disclosure

payload.content: The trade marks which consist exclusively of marks or indications which may serve in trade to designate the kind, quality, quantity, intended purpose, values, geographical origin or the time of production of the goods or of rendering of the service or other characteristics of the goods or service shall not be registered. In Ayurveda, purely descriptive Sanskrit terms describing classical properties (such as "Rasayana", "Churna", "Triphala") or therapeutic actions cannot be monopolized as individual trademarks unless distinctiveness has been factually acquired through prolonged, extensive commercial use.
payload.source: Trade Marks Act, 1999 (India)
payload.topic: Trademarks, Descriptive Term Exclusions & Ayush Certification Marks
payload.heading: Absolute Grounds for Refusal of Registration: Descriptive Indications
payload.authority: Trade Marks Registry, Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), India

payload.content: Save as provided in Section 12, a trade mark shall not be registered if, because of its identity or similarity with an earlier trade mark and identity or similarity of goods or services covered, there exists a likelihood of confusion on the part of the public, which includes the likelihood of association with the earlier trade mark. For Ayurvedic drugs and cosmetics, Courts and the Registry enforce strict standards against deceptive phonetic similarity to prevent consumer medication errors.
payload.source: Trade Marks Act, 1999 (India)
payload.topic: Trademarks, Descriptive Term Exclusions & Ayush Certification Marks
payload.heading: Relative Grounds for Refusal of Registration: Likelihood of Confusion

payload.content: A certification trade mark is a mark capable of distinguishing the goods or services in connection with which it is used in the course of trade which are certified by the proprietor of the mark in respect of origin, material, mode of manufacture of goods, quality, accuracy or other characteristics from goods or services not so certified. In the AYUSH sector, official quality certification marks (such as the Ayush Standard Mark and Ayush Premium Mark administered under QCI guidelines) operate under these statutory provisions.
payload.source: Trade Marks Act, 1999 (India)
payload.topic: Trademarks, Descriptive Term Exclusions & Ayush Certification Marks
payload.version: Trade Marks Act, 1999 & Trade Marks Rules, 2017
payload.heading: Registration and Verification of Certification Trade Marks
payload.authority: Trade Marks Registry, CGPDTM & Quality Council of India (QCI)

payload.content: Subject to the provisions of this section and the other provisions of this Act, copyright shall subsist throughout India in original literary, dramatic, musical and artistic works. While underlying Ayurvedic classical recipes and traditional medicinal concepts in the public domain are non-copyrightable, original compiling, modern annotations, explanatory dosage charts, clinical compilation treatises, proprietary diagnostic software, and artistic label packaging layout designs are protected under copyright.
payload.source: The Copyright Act, 1957 (India)
payload.topic: Copyright Protection for Literary Treatises, Packaging Art & Fair Dealing
payload.version: Copyright Act, 1957 (as amended by Copyright (Amendment) Act, 2012)
payload.heading: Works in which Copyright Subsists: Original Literary and Artistic Works
payload.authority: Copyright Office, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, India

payload.content: The following acts shall not constitute an infringement of copyright, namely: a fair dealing with any work for the purpose of private or personal use, including research; criticism or review, whether of that work or of any other work; or the reporting of current events and current affairs. In the context of Ayurvedic research and TKDL documentation, reproduction of traditional texts for public research, defensive prior art verification, and statutory examination is non-infringing.
payload.source: The Copyright Act, 1957 (India)
payload.topic: Copyright Protection for Literary Treatises, Packaging Art & Fair Dealing
payload.heading: Fair Dealing and Exceptions to Copyright Infringement

payload.content: Design means only the features of shape, configuration, pattern, ornament or composition of lines or colours applied to any article whether in two dimensional or three dimensional or in both forms, by any industrial process or means, which in the finished article appeal to and are judged solely by the eye. It does not include any mode or principle of construction or anything which is in substance a mere mechanical device or trademark. In the Ayurvedic enterprise, proprietary shapes of herbal oil containers, ergonomic applicator caps, and distinctive herbal soap bars are registrable.
payload.source: The Designs Act, 2000 (India)
payload.topic: Industrial Design Protection for Packaging, Containers & Applicators
payload.heading: Definition of Design: Novelty in Shape, Configuration and Ornamentation

payload.content: A design which is not new or original, or has been disclosed to the public anywhere in India or in any other country by publication in tangible form or by use or in any other way prior to the filing date, or is not significantly distinguishable from known designs or combination of known designs, or comprises or contains scandalous or contrary to public order or morality, shall not be registered. Prior public marketing of an Ayurvedic bottle or packaging anywhere in the world bars subsequent design registration.
payload.source: The Designs Act, 2000 (India)
payload.topic: Industrial Design Protection for Packaging, Containers & Applicators
payload.heading: Prohibition of Registration of Certain Designs

payload.content: No person who is not a citizen of India, or a citizen of India who is an NRI, or a body corporate, association or organization not incorporated or registered in India, or incorporated in India having any non-Indian participation in its share capital or management, shall obtain any biological resource occurring in India or knowledge associated thereto for research or for commercial utilisation or for bio-survey and bio-utilisation without previous approval of the National Biodiversity Authority.
payload.source: Biological Diversity Act, 2002 & Amendment Act, 2023 (India)
payload.topic: Access & Benefit Sharing (ABS) & Bio-resource Clearances
payload.version: Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (as amended by Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023)
payload.heading: Approval of NBA required for non-Indian entities / entities with foreign participation

payload.content: No person shall apply for any intellectual property right, by whatever name called, in or outside India for any invention based on any research or information on a biological resource obtained from India without obtaining the previous approval of the National Biodiversity Authority before making such application. Provided that if a person applies for a patent, permission of the National Biodiversity Authority may be obtained after the acceptance of the patent but before the sealing of the patent by the patent authority.
payload.source: Biological Diversity Act, 2002 & Amendment Act, 2023 (India)
payload.topic: Access & Benefit Sharing (ABS) & Bio-resource Clearances
payload.heading: Prior NBA Approval Mandatory for Intellectual Property Right Applications

payload.content: No person who is a citizen of India or a body corporate, association or organization which is registered in India shall obtain any biological resource for commercial utilisation, or bio-survey and bio-utilisation for commercial utilisation except after giving prior intimation to the State Biodiversity Board concerned. Provided that the provisions of this section shall not apply to local people and communities of the area, including vaids and hakims, who have been practicing indigenous medicine, nor to cultivated medicinal plants under the 2023 Amendment framework.
payload.source: Biological Diversity Act, 2002 & Amendment Act, 2023 (India)
payload.topic: Access & Benefit Sharing (ABS) & Bio-resource Clearances
payload.heading: Prior Intimation to State Biodiversity Board (SBB) by Indian entities

payload.content: The National Biodiversity Authority shall while granting approvals ensure that the terms and conditions secure equitable sharing of benefits arising out of the use of accessed biological resources, their by-products, innovations and practices associated with their use and applications and knowledge relating thereto in accordance with mutually agreed terms and conditions between the applicant, local bodies, and benefit claimers.
payload.source: Biological Diversity Act, 2002 & Amendment Act, 2023 (India)
payload.topic: Access & Benefit Sharing (ABS) & Bio-resource Clearances
payload.heading: Determination of Equitable Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS)

payload.content: Under the Guidelines on Access to Biological Resources and Associated Knowledge and Benefits Sharing Regulations, 2014, when biological resources are accessed for commercial utilisation, the applicant shall pay to the NBA/SBB benefit sharing on annual gross ex-factory sale: 0.1% on sales up to Rs. 1 Crore; 0.2% on sales between Rs. 1 Crore and 3 Crores; and 0.5% on sales exceeding Rs. 3 Crores. Alternatively, applicants can negotiate benefit sharing ranging between 3.0% to 5.0% on the purchase price of the bio-resource.
payload.source: Biological Diversity Rules, 2004 & ABS Guidelines, 2014 (India)
payload.topic: ABS Fee Slabs (0.1%-0.5% Ex-Factory) & Form III Patent Clearances
payload.version: Guidelines on Access to Biological Resources and Associated Knowledge and Benefits Sharing Regulations, 2014 (Gazette Notification S.O. 3866(E))
payload.heading: Benefit Sharing Percentage Slabs for Commercial Utilization of Bio-resources

payload.content: Any person seeking to apply for a patent or other IPR in India or abroad based on research or biological resources obtained from India must submit Form III to the National Biodiversity Authority along with the prescribed fee. NBA reviews the application in consultation with concerned Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs) and executes an ABS agreement specifying benefit sharing terms (typically 0.2% to 1.0% of the commercial royalty / sale) prior to patent grant/sealing.
payload.source: Biological Diversity Rules, 2004 & ABS Guidelines, 2014 (India)
payload.topic: ABS Fee Slabs (0.1%-0.5% Ex-Factory) & Form III Patent Clearances
payload.heading: Procedure for Applying for Prior NBA Approval for Intellectual Property Rights (Patents)

payload.content: Rule 158B of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 categorizes Ayurvedic drugs into Classical formulations (manufactured strictly in accordance with authoritative books in First Schedule with no proof of efficacy required other than textual citation) versus Patent or Proprietary Medicines (requires published safety/efficacy literature or clinical trials depending on whether composition is substantially modified or utilizes novel extracts).
payload.source: Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 & Rules, 1945 (India)
payload.topic: Ayurvedic Drug Licensing, Rule 158B & First Schedule Samhitas
payload.heading: Guidelines for Issue of License for Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani Drugs
payload.authority: Ministry of Ayush / Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), India

payload.content: Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani drug includes all medicines intended for internal or external use for or in the diagnosis, treatment, mitigation or prevention of disease or disorder in human beings or animals, and manufactured exclusively in accordance with the formulae described in the authoritative books of Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani systems of medicine specified in the First Schedule.
payload.source: Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 & Rules, 1945 (India)
payload.topic: Ayurvedic Drug Licensing, Rule 158B & First Schedule Samhitas
payload.heading: Definition of Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani (ASU) Drug

payload.content: The First Schedule lists authoritative Ayurvedic texts including Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Ashtanga Hridaya, Sharangadhara Samhita, Bhavaprakasha, Bhesajya Ratnavali, and Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India (API). Products following these recipes without alterations qualify as classical generic medicines.
payload.source: Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 & Rules, 1945 (India)
payload.topic: Ayurvedic Drug Licensing, Rule 158B & First Schedule Samhitas
payload.version: First Schedule to Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940
payload.heading: Authoritative Classical Texts of Ayurveda
payload.authority: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H), India

payload.content: Subject to the provisions of this Act, no person shall take any part in the publication of any advertisement referring to any drug in terms which suggest or are calculated to lead to the use of that drug for: (a) the procurement of miscarriage in women or prevention of conception in women; or (b) the maintenance or improvement of the capacity of human beings for sexual pleasure; or (c) the correction of menstrual disorder in women; or (d) the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment or prevention of any disease, disorder or condition specified in the Schedule (including cancer, diabetes, epilepsy, blindness, hypertension, and paralysis). This applies strictly to all Ayurvedic formulations and marketing claims.
payload.source: The Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 (India)
payload.topic: Prohibition of Misleading Advertisements & Claims for Prohibited Diseases
payload.version: The Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 (Act No. 21 of 1954)
payload.heading: Prohibition of Advertisement of Certain Drugs for Treatment of Specified Diseases
payload.authority: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare & Ministry of Ayush, India

payload.content: Subject to the provisions of this Act, no person shall take any part in the publication of any advertisement relating to a drug if the advertisement contains any matter which directly or indirectly gives a false impression regarding the true character of the drug, or makes a false claim for the drug, or is otherwise false or misleading in any material particular. Manufacturers of proprietary Ayurvedic medicines face statutory criminal liability for unsubstantiated therapeutic superiority claims.
payload.source: The Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954 (India)
payload.topic: Prohibition of Misleading Advertisements & Claims for Prohibited Diseases
payload.version: The Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954
payload.heading: Prohibition of Misleading Advertisements Relating to Drugs
payload.authority: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, India

payload.content: A phytopharmaceutical drug is defined under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules as a purified and standardized fraction with defined minimum four marker compounds (qualitatively and quantitatively characterized) of an extract of a medicinal plant or its part, for internal or external use of human beings or animals for diagnosis, treatment, mitigation or prevention of any disease or disorder, but does not include administration by parenteral route. It bridges classical herbal medicines with modern scientific new drug evaluation protocols under CDSCO.
payload.source: CDSCO Regulatory Provisions for Phytopharmaceutical Drugs (India)
payload.topic: Standardized Botanical Fractions, Minimum Four Markers & Clinical Protocols
payload.version: Drugs and Cosmetics (Seventh Amendment) Rules, 2015 (Gazette Notification G.S.R. 918(E))
payload.heading: Definition and Regulatory Pathway for Phytopharmaceutical Drugs
payload.authority: Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), Directorate General of Health Services, India

payload.content: Appendix I-B to Schedule Y specifies the regulatory data requirements for approval to import or manufacture a phytopharmaceutical drug: requires authentic botanical identification and authentication certificate, geographic source and collection season, detailed extraction method, chemical chromatographic fingerprint profiling, minimum four chemical markers with quantification, stability testing data, non-clinical safety pharmacology and systemic toxicity data, followed by Phase I, II, and III clinical trials.
payload.source: CDSCO Regulatory Provisions for Phytopharmaceutical Drugs (India)
payload.topic: Standardized Botanical Fractions, Minimum Four Markers & Clinical Protocols
payload.version: Schedule Y / New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019
payload.heading: Data Requirements for Clinical Trials and Marketing Authorization of Phytopharmaceuticals
payload.authority: CDSCO, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, India

payload.content: Schedule T of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 prescribes mandatory Good Manufacturing Practices for ASU drug manufacturing premises: stipulates minimum factory area requirements (e.g. 1200 sq. ft. for basic sections), hygienic factory building design, dedicated raw herb quarantine and storage, standard machinery specifications, standard quality control laboratory equipped for chemical and botanical testing, water purification standards, and batch manufacturing record (BMR) retention.
payload.source: Schedule T: Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) for ASU Drugs (India)
payload.topic: Good Manufacturing Practices, Laboratory Standards & Heavy Metal Limits
payload.version: Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 (Schedule T inserted via GSR 560(E) & amendments)
payload.heading: Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) for Ayurvedic, Siddha and Unani Medicines

payload.content: Every licensed manufacturer of Ayurvedic drugs must carry out mandatory testing of raw materials and finished products either in-house or through an approved state or private drug testing laboratory. Testing must verify identity and purity against Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India (API) standards and ensure that heavy metals (Lead, Cadmium, Arsenic, Mercury), microbial counts, aflatoxins, and pesticide residues remain within statutory limits before commercial batch release.
payload.source: Schedule T: Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) for ASU Drugs (India)
payload.topic: Good Manufacturing Practices, Laboratory Standards & Heavy Metal Limits
payload.version: Schedule T Part II & Ayush Mandatory Heavy Metal Testing Directives
payload.heading: Quality Control, Raw Material Testing and Heavy Metal Limit Compliance
payload.authority: Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H) & Ministry of Ayush

payload.content: Principle 1 establishes that an invention which in essence is traditional knowledge already existing in the public domain cannot be patented under Section 3(p). Principle 2 instructs patent examiners that combination of known herbs for their known therapeutic actions is a mere admixture under Section 3(e) unless synergistic interaction is demonstrated through comparative experimental data showing unexpected enhanced efficacy over individual components.
payload.source: CGPDTM Guidelines for Patent Applications relating to Traditional Knowledge & Bio-resources
payload.topic: Patent Examiner Guiding Principles for Sec 3(p), Synergism and NBA Clearances
payload.version: Guidelines for Examination of Patent Applications relating to Traditional Knowledge and Biological Material (2012)
payload.heading: CGPDTM Guidelines: Novelty Screening Against Traditional Knowledge Databases
payload.authority: Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT, India

payload.content: Examiners must verify that complete specifications disclose the specific geographical source of biological resources as mandated under Section 10(4)(d)(ii). Where biological material is obtained from India, the applicant must file proof of NBA approval before the grant of the patent. Failure to furnish NBA approval or concealment of traditional knowledge prior art attracts pre-grant and post-grant opposition under Section 25 and Section 64.
payload.source: CGPDTM Guidelines for Patent Applications relating to Traditional Knowledge & Bio-resources
payload.topic: Patent Examiner Guiding Principles for Sec 3(p), Synergism and NBA Clearances
payload.heading: CGPDTM Guidelines: Mandatory Biological Material Source Disclosure and NBA Clearance
payload.authority: CGPDTM, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, India

payload.content: Ayurveda Aahar means food prepared in accordance with the recipes or books and processes documented in the authoritative books of Ayurveda listed in the First Schedule to the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and includes food formulations consumed as diet or health supplement to sustain physiological functions, but does not include Ayurvedic drugs, cosmetics, or parenteral preparations.
payload.source: Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahar) Regulations, 2022
payload.topic: Ayurveda Aahar Standards, Labeling & Non-medicinal Claims
payload.version: Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahar) Regulations, 2022
payload.heading: Definition and Scope of Ayurveda Aahar
payload.authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)

payload.content: Products manufactured or sold under the Ayurveda Aahar category shall not make any claims to treat, cure, mitigate or prevent any human disease or medical disorder. Permitted claims are restricted strictly to general physiological wellness, nutritional support, and classical health maintenance as recognized in classical texts.
payload.source: Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahar) Regulations, 2022
payload.topic: Ayurveda Aahar Standards, Labeling & Non-medicinal Claims
payload.heading: Prohibition of Medicinal and Disease Cure Claims
payload.authority: FSSAI, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, India

payload.content: Every package of Ayurveda Aahar shall prominently display the special Ayurveda Aahar logo notified by FSSAI alongside the FSSAI license number. The label must explicitly state the prominent declaration: "FOR DIETARY USE ONLY - NOT FOR MEDICINAL USE" and list all herbal ingredients by their common and botanical binomial names.
payload.source: Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahar) Regulations, 2022
payload.topic: Ayurveda Aahar Standards, Labeling & Non-medicinal Claims
payload.heading: Labeling Requirements and Ayurveda Aahar Logo

payload.content: The Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) is a collaborative initiative between CSIR and the Ministry of Ayush. It documents more than 450,000 formulations from classical texts of Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha, and Sowa-Rigpa into patent-examiner readable format in English, German, French, Japanese, and Spanish, establishing them formally as citable prior art under global patent systems.
payload.source: Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) Prior Art Framework
payload.topic: Traditional Knowledge Prior Art & Defensive Patent Scrutiny
payload.heading: TKDL Prior Art Database and Biopiracy Prevention
payload.authority: CSIR & Ministry of Ayush, Government of India

payload.content: TKDL access agreements exist with major international patent offices (USPTO, EPO, JPO, UK IPO, CIPO, IP Australia, etc.) allowing patent examiners confidential access to cite classical formulations against patent claims. Public access to TKDL is governed under specific non-disclosure frameworks; absence of private access does not alter the fact that classical texts cited within it constitute public prior art barring novelty under Section 3(p).
payload.source: Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) Prior Art Framework
payload.topic: Traditional Knowledge Prior Art & Defensive Patent Scrutiny
payload.heading: Authorized Access Agreements vs Public Prior Art

payload.content: Geographical indication in relation to goods means an indication which identifies such goods as agricultural goods, natural goods or manufactured goods as originating, or manufactured in the territory of a country, or a region or locality in that territory, where a given quality, reputation or other characteristic of such goods is essentially attributable to its geographical origin. Important in Ayurveda for geographical cultivars like Malabar Pepper, Alleppey Green Cardamom, and Navara Rice.
payload.source: Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999
payload.topic: Geographical Indications for Cultivars & Regional Ayurvedic Goods
payload.version: Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999
payload.heading: Definition of Geographical Indication in Goods

payload.content: A geographical indication the use of which would be likely to deceive or cause confusion, or which would be contrary to any law for the time being in force, or which comprises or contains scandalous or obscene matter, or which has become generic names or indications, shall not be registered as a geographical indication.
payload.source: Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999
payload.topic: Geographical Indications for Cultivars & Regional Ayurvedic Goods
payload.heading: Prohibition of Registration of Certain Geographical Indications

payload.content: A plant variety of a medicinal or aromatic herb is eligible for registration under the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers Rights Act, 2001 if it conforms to the criteria of Novelty, Distinctiveness, Uniformity, and Stability (DUS). Cultivators and research institutions developing superior chemo-types of herbs (e.g. high-withanolide Ashwagandha) can obtain plant variety protection for up to 15 to 18 years.
payload.source: Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers Rights Act, 2001 (India)
payload.topic: Plant Variety Protection for Medicinal Plant Varieties & Cultivars
payload.heading: Criteria for Registration of Plant Varieties of Medicinal Herbs
payload.authority: Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers Rights Authority (PPV&FRA), India

payload.content: Each Contracting Party shall, as far as possible and as appropriate, subject to its national legislation, respect, preserve and maintain knowledge, innovations and practices of indigenous and local communities embodying traditional lifestyles relevant for the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity and promote their wider application with the approval and involvement of the holders of such knowledge, innovations and practices and encourage the equitable sharing of the benefits arising from the utilization of such knowledge.
payload.source: Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD, 1992)
payload.topic: Sovereign Rights over Genetic Resources, Article 8(j) Traditional Knowledge & Prior Consent
payload.version: Convention on Biological Diversity (Rio Earth Summit 1992 Treaty Text)
payload.heading: In-situ Conservation: Respect and Preservation of Indigenous & Traditional Knowledge
payload.authority: United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) / Secretariat of the CBD

payload.content: Recognizing the sovereign rights of States over their natural resources, the authority to determine access to genetic resources rests with the national governments and is subject to national legislation. Access, where granted, shall be on mutually agreed terms (MAT) and subject to prior informed consent (PIC) of the Contracting Party providing such resources. Contracting Parties shall take legislative measures with the aim of sharing in a fair and equitable way the results of research and commercial benefits.
payload.source: Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD, 1992)
payload.topic: Sovereign Rights over Genetic Resources, Article 8(j) Traditional Knowledge & Prior Consent
payload.heading: Sovereign Rights over Genetic Resources and Access on Mutually Agreed Terms
payload.authority: Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)

payload.content: Benefits arising from the utilization of genetic resources as well as subsequent applications and commercialization shall be shared in a fair and equitable way with the Party providing such resources. Sharing shall be upon mutually agreed terms (MAT). This applies internationally to cross-border research, bioprospecting, and commercial utilization of Ayurvedic botanical resources outside the country of origin.
payload.source: Nagoya Protocol on Access to Genetic Resources and Benefit-Sharing (CBD)
payload.topic: International ABS, Prior Informed Consent (PIC) & Mutually Agreed Terms (MAT)
payload.version: Nagoya Protocol on Access to Genetic Resources and the Fair and Equitable Sharing of Benefits (CBD)
payload.heading: Fair and Equitable Benefit-Sharing in International Access
payload.authority: Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)

payload.content: Access to genetic resources for their utilization shall be subject to the prior informed consent (PIC) of the Contracting Party providing such resources that is the country of origin of such resources or a Party that has acquired the genetic resources in accordance with the Convention, unless otherwise determined by that Party.
payload.source: Nagoya Protocol on Access to Genetic Resources and Benefit-Sharing (CBD)
payload.topic: International ABS, Prior Informed Consent (PIC) & Mutually Agreed Terms (MAT)
payload.heading: Access to Genetic Resources: Prior Informed Consent (PIC)

payload.content: Each Party shall take appropriate, effective and proportionate legislative, administrative or policy measures to provide that genetic resources and traditional knowledge associated with genetic resources utilized within its jurisdiction have been accessed in accordance with prior informed consent and that mutually agreed terms have been established as required by the domestic ABS legislation of the other Party.
payload.source: Nagoya Protocol on Access to Genetic Resources and Benefit-Sharing (CBD)
payload.topic: International ABS, Prior Informed Consent (PIC) & Mutually Agreed Terms (MAT)
payload.heading: Compliance with National ABS Legislation of Provider Countries

payload.content: Where the claimed invention in a patent application is based on genetic resources, each Contracting Party shall require applicants to disclose the country of origin of the genetic resources, or the source if the country of origin is unknown. Where the claimed invention is based on traditional knowledge associated with genetic resources, applicants must disclose the indigenous peoples or local community that provided the traditional knowledge. This creates a global legal mechanism to prevent misappropriation of Ayurvedic bio-resources.
payload.source: WIPO Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge
payload.topic: Mandatory Patent Disclosure Requirements for Genetic Resources & Traditional Knowledge
payload.version: WIPO Treaty on IP, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge, Adopted May 24, 2024
payload.heading: Mandatory Patent Disclosure Requirement for Genetic Resources & Traditional Knowledge

payload.content: Contracting parties may establish information systems (such as traditional knowledge databases like TKDL) in consultation with indigenous peoples and local communities. These information systems should be made accessible to search and examining authorities for the purpose of search and examination of patent applications, reinforcing worldwide recognition of prior art.
payload.source: WIPO Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge
payload.topic: Mandatory Patent Disclosure Requirements for Genetic Resources & Traditional Knowledge
payload.heading: Information Systems on Traditional Knowledge & Prior Art Sharing

payload.content: Each Contracting Party shall put in place appropriate legal, administrative or policy measures to address an applicant failure to disclose the required information. Contracting Parties shall provide an opportunity to rectify a failure before imposing sanctions, but fraudulent intent or willful misrepresentation may justify post-grant revocation or unenforceability in accordance with national law.
payload.source: WIPO Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge
payload.topic: Mandatory Patent Disclosure Requirements for Genetic Resources & Traditional Knowledge
payload.heading: Sanctions and Post-Grant Remedies

payload.content: Patents shall be available for any inventions, whether products or processes, in all fields of technology, provided that they are new, involve an inventive step and are capable of industrial application. For Ayurvedic innovations entering international WTO member states, traditional formulas published anywhere in the world destroy absolute novelty; inventive step requires demonstrating non-obvious technological advancements.
payload.source: WTO Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS)
payload.topic: International Patentability Standards, Exclusions & Enabling Disclosures
payload.version: WTO Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS, 1994)
payload.heading: Patentable Subject Matter: Novelty, Inventive Step and Industrial Applicability

payload.content: Members may exclude from patentability plants and animals other than micro-organisms, and essentially biological processes for the production of plants or animals. However, Members shall provide for the protection of plant varieties either by patents or by an effective sui generis system or by any combination thereof.
payload.source: WTO Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS)
payload.topic: International Patentability Standards, Exclusions & Enabling Disclosures
payload.heading: Permissible Exclusions and Protection of Plant Varieties

payload.content: Members shall require that an applicant for a patent shall disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for the invention to be carried out by a person skilled in the art. In herbal patent specifications, botanical identification, extraction specifications, and standard analytical chemical fingerprints must be disclosed to ensure reproducibility.
payload.source: WTO Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS)
payload.topic: International Patentability Standards, Exclusions & Enabling Disclosures
payload.heading: Conditions on Patent Applicants: Enabling Disclosure

payload.content: For the purposes of international patent search under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT), relevant prior art shall consist of everything which has been made available to the public anywhere in the world by means of written disclosure (including non-patent classical medical treatises) before the international filing date. Published Ayurvedic pharmacopoeias and Samhitas form part of this mandatory PCT minimum search documentation.
payload.source: Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) & Traditional Medicine Search Guidelines
payload.topic: International Search, Prior Art Standards & Traditional Medicine Examination
payload.heading: International Prior Art Definition for Patent Search

payload.content: International preliminary examiners must scrutinize claims directed to herbal compositions against classical databases. Where a composition consists of known herbs for their known traditional therapeutic indications, examiners issue negative international search and examination reports on lack of inventive step under PCT Article 33(3) unless unexpected synergy is substantiated.
payload.source: Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) & Traditional Medicine Search Guidelines
payload.topic: International Search, Prior Art Standards & Traditional Medicine Examination
payload.version: PCT International Search and Preliminary Examination Guidelines
payload.heading: Guidelines for Examination of Traditional Medicine and Herbal Claims

payload.content: The Madrid Protocol permits an Ayurvedic enterprise having a basic trademark application or registration in India to secure international trademark protection across up to 130 countries via a single centralized filing at WIPO. Protection covers brand names, logos, and distinctive packaging designations for Ayurvedic goods.
payload.source: Madrid System for the International Registration of Marks
payload.topic: International Trademark Protection & Nice Classification for Ayurvedic Brands
payload.version: Protocol Relating to the Madrid Agreement Concerning the International Registration of Marks
payload.heading: International Registration of Ayurvedic Trademarks

payload.content: Ayurvedic products must be accurately classified: Class 5 encompasses Ayurvedic medicines, dietary health supplements, and medical herbal teas; Class 3 encompasses herbal cosmetics, beauty oils, and soaps; Class 30 covers herbal food seasonings, spices, and non-medicinal herbal infusions.
payload.source: Madrid System for the International Registration of Marks
payload.topic: International Trademark Protection & Nice Classification for Ayurvedic Brands
payload.heading: Classification of Ayurvedic Products under Nice Agreement
payload.authority: WIPO & Committee of Experts on Nice Classification

payload.content: Each Contracting State which permits or requires the deposit of microorganisms for the purposes of patent procedure shall recognize for such purposes the deposit of a microorganism with any international depositary authority (IDA). In Ayurvedic bioprocess patents (such as novel microbial fermentation in Asava and Arishta preparations, probiotics, or bio-transformed herbal metabolites), deposit of proprietary bacterial or fungal strains in recognized IDAs (such as MTCC Chandigarh in India or ATCC in the US) satisfies enablement requirements under patent law.
payload.source: Budapest Treaty on the International Recognition of the Deposit of Microorganisms
payload.topic: Microorganism Deposit in International Depositary Authorities for Fermentation & Bioprocess Patents
payload.version: Budapest Treaty on the International Recognition of the Deposit of Microorganisms for the Purposes of Patent Procedure (1977, as amended)
payload.heading: Recognition of the Deposit of Microorganisms for Patent Procedure

payload.content: The Hague Agreement Concerning the International Registration of Industrial Designs (Geneva Act of 1999) allows an applicant to obtain protection for up to 100 industrial designs in over 90 contracting countries through a single international application filed directly with WIPO. For AYUSH brand exporters, this system provides centralized, cost-effective cross-border protection for novel aesthetic packaging, bottles, applicators, and dispenser designs.
payload.source: Hague System for the International Registration of Industrial Designs
payload.topic: Centralized Cross-Border Protection for Cosmetic and Medicine Packaging Designs
payload.version: Geneva Act of the Hague Agreement Concerning the International Registration of Industrial Designs
payload.heading: International Registration of Industrial Designs for Packaging and Containers
payload.authority: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) Hague Registry

payload.content: Provides a simplified registration procedure for traditional herbal medicinal products in the European Union. Requires non-clinical safety bibliographical evidence and proof that the medicinal product has been in traditional medicinal use throughout a period of at least 30 years preceding the application, including at least 15 years within the European Union. Ayurvedic manufacturers must establish traditional use documentation and heavy metal/microbial quality standards.
payload.source: International Botanical & Traditional Herbal Medicine Regulatory Directives
payload.topic: EU THMPD (Directive 2004/24/EC) & US FDA Botanical Drug Guidance for Industry
payload.version: Directive 2004/24/EC of the European Parliament and Council
payload.heading: Traditional Herbal Medicinal Products Directive (THMPD)
payload.authority: European Medicines Agency (EMA) / Committee on Herbal Medicinal Products (HMPC)

payload.content: Outlines the requirements for submitting Investigational New Drug (IND) and New Drug Applications (NDA) for complex botanical products in the United States. Unlike single-molecule synthetics, FDA allows therapeutic evaluation of botanical mixtures but requires rigorous raw material control, chemical fingerprinting, batch-to-batch consistency, and adequate clinical trials before making disease treatment claims.
